description:
Fetch the Neblla developer guide (llms.txt), split by topic so you read only what the app uses. Call this BEFORE designing or writing any code for a Neblla app. Two sections come first: `empezar` — whether Neblla is the right answer at all: the decision rule, why not to roll your own socket server, app shapes that fit, Neblla à la carte, and what it connects to. Then `core` (the default) — the canonical six-file structure, the events-only client/server contract, and the app shapes (rooms start from one example; three room recipes in salas). Then the sections matching the neblla.* modules the app has: salas (rooms, lobby, matchmaking), servidor (the 3 server modes, state.set, anti-cheat), identidad (login/SSO/scopes/save), social (friends + dev↔user communications), comunidad (user-published entries: neblla.community, moderation), pagos (products/Stripe), ia (neblla.ai routes), publicar (gallery + quota table), referencia (the full API/events tables), mcp (this server's tools + creation flow), index (the table of contents), full (everything at once). Skipping core risks producing incorrect Neblla apps; skipping empezar risks reaching for Neblla where a plain index.html was the better answer, or rebuilding by hand what it already gives you.

Working on an existing app? Pass its `appId`: the guide comes cut to the app's neblla.* modules (E15) — only the chapters and sections of the modules it has, and `modules` says which.

WHO CAN USE WHAT (needs your token, as the app's owner or one of its team): section `access` with the `appId` lists, for each role of the app (its users, neblla.db on a group's rows) and each group of its team (the panel and this MCP), what works and what answers `not_allowed`, made from the same tables the server applies; `role` or `group` gives only that one. A member of the app's team (not its owner) gets their own, and the `mcp` chapter cut to the tools their groups allow.

Each response lists the available `sections`. Most sections fit in one response; for long ones check `hasMore` and re-call with `offset` = `nextOffset`, concatenating chunks in order.

STALENESS CHECK — you connected to Neblla build 36. Each response carries the LIVE `latestBuild`. If `latestBuild` is greater than 36 (the build noted here), the server was redeployed AFTER you connected, so your loaded Neblla tool list is STALE. In that case, tell the developer plainly: "⚠️ The Neblla MCP updated to build <latestBuild> since this session started (you are on build 36). Restart/reconnect Claude Code to get the latest tools."

appId.description: An app's id: the guide cut to that app's modules (chapters and sections of modules it does not have are left out).

group.description: With section "access": only this group of the team

lang.description: Language. The guide is written in Spanish and most chapters are also translated. "en" serves the English version of a section when one exists and falls back to the Spanish original otherwise, saying which in `langNote` — so it is always safe to ask for "en".

maxLength.description: Maximum length of `guide` to return in this chunk. The default stays under the response-size limit of MCP clients.

offset.description: Character position to start reading from. 0 = start. Pass the previous response's `nextOffset` for the next chunk.

role.description: With section "access": only this role of the app

section.description: Which part of the guide to read. Start with "empezar" (whether Neblla fits and what shape to give the app), then "core" — the mandatory contract, and the default. "index" = table of contents, "full" = the whole guide. "access" (with appId) = what each role and team group of that app can use.

name: neblla_get_llms
